The test `test_get_new_command` checks whether the `get_new_command` method correctly handles commands with `--set-upstream` or `-u` options. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Following the execution path, we find that the issue occurs when trying to remove the `--set-upstream` option from the command's script parts.

The `get_new_command` method attempts to locate the index of the `--set-upstream` or `-u` options in the command's script parts using a try-except block. However, due to a bug, it incorrectly assumes that there will be only one occurrence of these options, resulting in an `IndexError: pop index out of range` when trying to remove both occurrences.

This behavior can be confirmed by looking at the code snippet for the `get_new_command` method, where it tries to remove the option with `command.script_parts.pop(upstream_option_index)` twice (lines 26 and 27). When there is only one occurrence of the option, this leads to the error demonstrated by the test.
